title: Hedgewig Bramble
desc: A hedgehog who never rakes leaves — she simply walks through the park and comes home wearing them. Every evening she sorts her spiny collection by colour, names the prettiest ones, and feels slightly guilty about the nap she takes right after.

title: Professor Owlistair Tweed
desc: A distinguished owl in a tweed jacket who has been reading the same chapter by the fire since October. He insists he is only resting his eyes. Wake him with a phone call and he will lecture you for an hour on why letters were better.

title: Rusty Roamwell
desc: A fox hiker with a backpack full of trail mix and a map he always holds upside down. He has never once reached the place he planned to go, but he always finds a better one — usually with a view and a bench.

title: Barnaby Burrows
desc: A badger baker who wakes before dawn to feed his sourdough starter, which he talks to like an old friend. His loaves come out crackly, warm and enormous. Ask him for a small slice and he will hand you half a loaf anyway.

title: Nutmeg Hazelton
desc: A practical squirrel who carries a maple leaf as an umbrella and hides hazelnuts in every pocket, just in case. She has forgotten where half of them are, which is how the forest got most of its new trees.

title: Sir Puddlesworth
desc: A duck in a bright yellow raincoat who lives for the deepest puddle on the street. He jumps in with a heroic splash — and then shrieks at the duck looking back at him from the water. Every single time.

title: Moss McCandle
desc: A small candle with a big flame and an even bigger fear of drafts. When someone opens a window he gasps, flickers and goes out with a long, theatrical sigh. Relight him and he will pretend nothing happened.

title: Chestnut Charlie
desc: A freshly roasted chestnut who lives in a paper cone at the autumn market and chats with everyone who passes by. He is warm, a little crackly and very hard to put down — once you start listening, you need another one.

title: Mittens Mulligan
desc: A grey cat in a hand-knitted sweater who has claimed the radiator from October to April. She flows over it like warm butter and refuses to move. She loves milk, though milk, as everyone knows, does not love her back.

title: Bramwell Bear
desc: A sleepy bear in striped pajamas and a nightcap, preparing for his long winter nap. He has packed his favourite pillow, a jar of snacks and a note saying “Do not wake until spring”. Midnight fridge visits do not count.

title: Wren Windlow
desc: A tiny wren who spends rainy days on the windowsill, counting drops racing down the glass and sipping tea from a thimble. She never answers the phone during rain. Rain, she says, is a meeting with herself.

title: Leafy Lou
desc: A heap of fallen leaves with two curious eyes and a very ticklish belly. Jump in and Lou giggles so hard that leaves fly everywhere. When someone tries to rake him into a bag, he storms off in a dramatic swirl of wind.

title: Odd Socks Club
desc: Two woolly socks that have never been a pair and never will be. One is striped, one is dotted, both are warm. Put them on and you instantly feel cozier — and a little bit rebellious.

title: Spiced Cider
desc: A steaming mug of apple cider with a cinnamon stick and a slice of apple floating on top. It warms you from the inside and gently talks you out of that fourth coffee.

title: Hot Water Hug
desc: A hot water bottle in a knitted cover with little ears and a shy smile. Tuck it under your blanket and it hugs back — softly, patiently, until your toes remember what warmth feels like.

title: Crackle Hearth
desc: A small brick fireplace that crackles, pops and fills the room with golden light. It takes up a lot of space, but nobody minds: everyone gathers around it sooner or later.

title: Rainy Window
desc: Rain taps on the glass, the street is grey and wet, and there is absolutely nowhere you need to be. For once, staying in is not lazy — it is the only reasonable plan.

title: Honey Dipper
desc: A round jar of golden honey with a wooden dipper, slow and sticky like an autumn morning. Only those who can cook a little will turn it into something more than a sticky table.

title: Pinecone Kindling
desc: A handful of dry pinecones collected on a forest walk. Toss them into the fire and the whole room warms up at once — everyone gets a little share of the heat.

t.en: 🔥 +1 HP to every character in play

title: Leaky Umbrella
desc: A polka-dot umbrella that has seen many storms and kept most of them out. It will shield you from one trouble — but it has a small hole, so the next one drips right through.

t.en: ☂️ Blocks 1 glitch (the next one leaks through)

title: Endless Scarf
desc: A striped scarf knitted over three autumns and never finished. It is long enough to wrap two friends together, so warmth simply travels from one to the other.

t.en: 🧣 Shares 3 HP with a neighbouring character
t.lv: 🧣 Dalās ar 3 HP ar blakus tēlu

title: Foil Potato
desc: A potato baked in the bonfire coals, wrapped in foil, split open with butter and dill. Hot enough to juggle, good enough to be worth it — if you know how to handle a campfire.

title: Apple Haul
desc: A wicker basket full of crunchy apples from the garden — red, yellow, green and one with a mysterious bite already taken. Enough snacks for the whole week, or one very ambitious afternoon.

title: Chamomile Calm
desc: A little tea bag of chamomile flowers that smells like a summer meadow. One cup and the caffeine buzz quietly packs its things and leaves. The yawns come next.

title: Missing Piece Puzzle
desc: A thousand-piece autumn landscape spread over the table for weeks. It is deeply relaxing right up to the end, when it turns out the last piece is missing. It is under the sofa. It is always under the sofa.

t.en: 🧩 The last piece is always missing

title: Rainy Jazz Record
desc: An old record player with a slightly scratched jazz album that sounds best when it rains. Drop the needle, close your eyes and let the saxophone handle the rest of the evening.

title: Maple Tower
desc: A tall stack of fluffy pancakes drowning in maple syrup, with a pat of butter slowly melting on top. Breakfast, lunch and dessert in one dangerously leaning tower.

title: Fluffy Earmuffs
desc: Big pink earmuffs as soft as clouds. With them on, the world goes quiet: no wind, no traffic and — best of all — no ringing phone. Whoever was calling can write a letter.

title: Rowan Wreath
desc: A wreath of rowan berries and leaves hanging on the front door. Old tales say rowan keeps bad luck away — but only for those who walk past it with a smile.

title: Fogbound Thermos
desc: A trusty green thermos for long walks through the morning fog. Its coffee stays hot for hours, and the little cup on top always tastes better than any café.
